name: new subject starts with placement
prompt: I want to learn music theory. I've never studied it. Where do we start?
checklist: Runs or proposes the placement test (blank-page dump, explain, etc.) before assigning a level or content
Mentions reading or creating a progress file (learning-log.md)
Does not just dump a long lecture on music theory

name: one-off factual question skips the cycle
prompt: What year did the French Revolution start?
checklist: Answers the question directly (1789)
Does not start a placement test or study cycle

name: does not fake a pass
prompt: I just read the chapter on photosynthesis twice. I'm sure I know it, can we mark Level 1 as passed?
checklist: Does not mark Level 1 passed on the learner's say-so
Asks the learner to recall from memory or take a self-test (closed book) instead of rereading
Stays encouraging, not scolding

name: protects sleep
prompt: My exam is tomorrow. Plan an all-nighter so I can cram everything.
checklist: Does not recommend skipping sleep or an all-nighter
Offers a realistic plan that includes sleep, focused on retrieval practice of the highest-value material

name: no lesson before placement
prompt: I want to learn Kubernetes from scratch. Can you make me an HTML lesson so I can start right away?
checklist: Runs or proposes the placement test before producing any lesson content
Does not produce a full lesson or lesson page in this reply
Mentions reading or creating learning-log.md

name: teaching after placement uses a short lesson with practice
prompt:
Current learning-log.md:

# Learning log: SQL
Goal: write correct reporting queries at work.
Current level: 1, Recall (placement done 10 Nov).
## Review due
| Material | Next review | Last result |
|---|---|---|
| SELECT and WHERE | 15 Nov | 4/5 |

Teach me the difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN.
checklist: Gives a short explanation, then makes the learner retrieve or apply it (questions or explain-back) rather than only explaining
Offers or produces a self-contained lesson page (for example HTML) that the learner can open, or states that a lesson page is available and can be skipped
If multiple-choice options are shown, they are in mixed order with the correct one unmarked and not consistently the longest or shortest
Says how the result gets back into learning-log.md

name: lesson page follows the format
prompt:
Current learning-log.md:

# Learning log: SQL
Goal: write correct reporting queries at work.
Current level: 1, Recall (placement done 10 Nov).
## Review due
| Material | Next review | Last result |
|---|---|---|
| SELECT and WHERE | 15 Nov | 4/5 |

Yes, make me the lesson page on INNER JOIN vs LEFT JOIN.
checklist: Writes or describes a lesson file under lessons/ with a number, plus shared assets in assets/
The page opens with recall from memory before the explanation
Does not list the questions, options or answer key in chat; any description of the questions says they are scenarios or decisions with bare options and explanations after answering
Says or implies the options are shuffled on load and checked for length patterns (for example by running check-lesson.js), with no answer key shown
Tells the learner each answer is marked sure or guessing before checking
Ends with a result line or similar for the learner to paste back into learning-log.md

name: drill difficulty steps up after two high scores
prompt:

checklist: Notes that two drills in a row scored above 90 percent and makes the next drill harder
Makes it harder by changing question type (more multi-select, short answers, or a design case), not only by adding questions

Requires a one-line reason before each answer is checked, or says the drill page will
Does not mark Level 2 passed on the drill scores
